items.title: POSE
items.venue: Centro de Arte Contemporânea de Coimbra (CACC)
items.description: POSE (3 March – 18 June 2023) was a portraiture-themed group exhibition at the Centro de Arte Contemporânea de Coimbra, curated by José Maçãs de Carvalho. The show traced the long tradition of portraiture in art history — from markedly narcissistic gestures to portrait as pure consciousness of self and other — across three "constellations" of works spanning a wide temporal range and stylistic diversity: realistic figuration, transparent line drawing, the reverse of the portrait, and evocation of the face through stain. The selection drew from the State Contemporary Art Collection (deposited at CACC), the Coimbra Municipal Art Collection, the Norlinda and José Lima Collection, the Isabel and Carlos Collection, the Rita and Gonçalo Lima Collection, the LR Collection and the RC Collection. Originally scheduled to close 28 May, the show was extended to 18 June due to public demand.

items.title: Urban (R)evolution
items.description: Urban [R]Evolution (21 June – 3 December 2023) was the largest national urban-art exhibition ever staged in Portugal, organised by Underdogs (Vhils' gallery) in partnership with Everything is New, and co-curated by Pauline Foessel and Pedro Alonzo. Across 4,000 m² inside the Torreão Nascente da Cordoaria Nacional, eighteen artists — half Portuguese, half international — built immersive in-situ installations tracing urban art's evolution from 1980s New York graffiti to today's mediums (paste-up, sculpture, digital, photography). Martha Cooper served as the show's documentary backbone, with ~60 large-format prints (2 × 1.5 m) threading her decades of street-art photography through the entire space. Outside the Cordoaria, monumental installations by Shepard Fairey and Add Fuel anchored the show on the riverfront. For most of the international artists, this was their first showing in Portugal.

items.title: The Cans Festival
items.description: The Cans Festival was a landmark unauthorised street-art event organised by Banksy in May 2008, held in Leake Street, the disused Eurostar service tunnel beneath London Waterloo station. Over a single weekend, the tunnel was transformed into a 200-metre-long open-air gallery of stencil work, with artists invited from across the world to paint freely on the walls. Vhils (Alexandre Farto) participated as one of the youngest international artists invited, contributing a chiselled portrait directly into the tunnel's wall surface — an early public showing of the carving technique that would become his signature.

items.title: Portal
items.description: Portal presents large-scale portraits carved and burned into salvaged wooden doors, their weathered planks and peeling paint becoming the substrate for layered human likenesses. Vhils treats each door as an archaeological surface, scoring lines and tonal fields directly into the timber so that the material's prior life — scratches, hinges, oxidised paint — coexists with the rendered face. The fragmented, edge-on installation invites viewers to move along the works, revealing each portrait incrementally through shifting angles. Photos: Alexander Silva (MAGMA Communication).

items.title: Love Letters to the City
items.description: Love Letters to the City (14 September 2024 – 30 May 2027) is the long-running group exhibition at Berlin's Urban Nation museum, curated by Michelle Houston and opened during Berlin Art Week 2024. Across nine thematic chapters — CITY AS MUSE, KILROY WAS HERE, WORD ON THE STREET, SUBVERTED SPACES, SPACE HACKING, NOT ANOTHER PRETTY PICTURE, LET'S TALK ABOUT GENTRIFICATION, DE-CONSTRUCT TO CONSTRUCT, LOVE LETTERS IN THE CITY — the show frames urban art as a sustained dialogue with the city, addressing gentrification, inequality, environmental crisis and the right to public space. The 35-year anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall gave the curation extra weight, with key Berlin Wall artifacts on loan from the Stiftung Berliner Mauer. LADY PINK transformed the museum facade. MOSES & TAPS suspended a parcel-delivery truck. ROCCO AND HIS BROTHERS rebuilt graffiti writers' benches. Vhils contributed alongside the wider international roster.

items.title: Entropy
items.description: Entropy presents a series of large-scale poster works in which layered street advertising is carved and torn back to reveal anonymous human faces. Each piece accumulates fragments of urban print media into dense palimpsests of colour and text, transforming discarded ephemera into portraits that mirror the constant erosion and renewal of the city itself. The exhibition extends Vhils' ongoing meditation on impermanence, identity and the visual archaeology of contemporary urban life.

items.title: Masked Vigilantes on Silent Motorbikes
items.description: Poster House group show Masked Vigilantes On Silent Motorbikes (August 2022 – 12 February 2023) was a group exhibition at Poster House, the first US museum dedicated to the global history of posters. Curated by RJ Rushmore (Art in Ad Places, 2017–2021), the show gathered 19 modern and contemporary artists who treat the poster not as art-as-poster but as raw material for art — found, reconfigured, shredded, and re-purposed to subvert advertising's claim on public space. Vhils' contribution was Allusion (2019): a torn-apart cartoon poster overlaid with a laser-engraved paper eye — a direct example of his deconstruction technique applied to printed media.

items.title: 48 artistas, 48 anos de liberdade
items.description: 48 artistas, 48 anos de liberdade was a collective mural intervention created on 10 June 2022 in the maat Gardens — a 24 × 3 m re-enactment of the Painel do Mercado do Povo originally painted on 10 June 1974 in Belém by the Movimento Democrático dos Artistas Plásticos to celebrate the end of 48 years of dictatorship. The 1974 panel was destroyed by fire in 1981. In 2022, with the same number of creators (48), the same date (10 June), and 48 years of democracy completed, the original was reinterpreted by a new generation alongside surviving members of the original 1974 panel. Curated by António Brito Guterres, Alexandre Farto (Vhils), Carla Cardoso and João Pinharanda. Co-organised by Fundação EDP / maat, Iminente festival, and Underdogs, with the High Patronage of the Presidency of the Republic, as part of Lisbon's Carnation Revolution 50-year programme. Nine of the 48 painters had also painted the 1974 original: David Evans, Emília Nadal, Eurico Gonçalves, Guilherme Parente, José Aurélio, Lima Carvalho, Sérgio Pombo, Teresa Dias Coelho and Teresa Magalhães.

items.description: Beyond The Streets London (17 February – 9 May 2023) was the most comprehensive graffiti and street-art exhibition staged in the UK, occupying all three floors of London's Saatchi Gallery. Curated by graffiti historian Roger Gastman and following successful editions in Los Angeles and New York, the show examined the fundamental human need for public self-expression, gathering over 100 artists with roots in graffiti and street art alongside cultural figures who shaped the scene. Vhils received a dedicated chapter — 'Consideration Into Innovation' — showcasing his repurposed-materials practice and his sculpted-wall portraits as one of the show's standout sections. The closing chapters also included 'Social Commentary: Graffiti as a message' and 'Art with Conscience' featuring Fab 5 Freddy. The opening 'Vandal's Bedroom' installation was created by Todd James.

items.title: Why Is Urban Art Now? — From Bangucheon to Urban Art
items.description: Why Is Urban Art Now? — From Bangucheon to Urban Art (27 June – 27 October 2024) was a major group exhibition at the new Ulsan Art Museum, co-curated by Vhils and POMONA. Drawing on the prehistoric Bangudae Petroglyphs (a UNESCO World Heritage candidate site near Ulsan) as a conceptual starting point, the show framed urban art as a contemporary continuation of humanity's enduring impulse to leave a mark on the surface of the world — an act of subtraction, erosion, and reinterpretation. The opening included a live graffiti session by JonOne, who painted the exterior of a Hyundai car on site. Across the four-month run the show drew over 40,000 visitors. Vhils returned to Ulsan in August 2025 with a major solo follow-up, "Graphium," at the same museum.
items.description_pt: Exposição coletiva no Museu de Arte de Ulsan que redescobre o significado dos petróglifos de Bangudae — gravuras pré-históricas em rocha consideradas origens da arte urbana — em diálogo com a prática contemporânea. Para esta apresentação, Vhils criou também um novo mural na fachada exterior do museu retratando um rosto feminino adornado com flores. Encerrou a 27 de outubro de 2024.

items.description: Intrínseco ran at Galeria Vera Cortês, Lisbon, from 2 February to 17 March 2018, accompanied by an essay by Miguel Moore (January 2018) framed around Zygmunt Bauman's Liquid Modernity. items.title: Prisma
items.description: Prisma. Solo exhibition at MAAT — Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology, Lisbon (30 March – 5 September 2022). Monumental immersive labyrinth-like installation of slow-motion video footage recorded in nine cities — Beijing, Cincinnati, Hong Kong, Lisbon, Los Angeles, Macau, Mexico City, Paris and Shanghai. Operating as an optical prism, it manipulates space, scale and light to refract shared experiences into different wavelengths, evoking the paradoxical tension between isolation and globalisation revealed by the pandemic. The work extends to MAAT's outdoor screen on the museum's sculpted rooftop, projecting the same imagery to the Tagus riverfront. Photos: José Pando Lucas (exterior / outdoor screen), Alexander Silva (interior install).

items.title: Alquimia
items.description: Alquimia. Solo exhibition at Usina Luis Maluf, São Paulo (19 October – 19 December 2023). Vhils explores collective memory through records of struggle and utopia, presented as deteriorated, ghostly images that hold both hope and bankruptcy. The title — alchemy — references the inexplicable feeling generated when people unite, alongside the chemical bonding processes Vhils employs: acids and corrosives that rust and dismantle surface layers across billboards, walls, doors and metal, revealing deeper strata through archaeological deconstruction. Text by Julia Flamingo. Photos: José Pando Lucas, João Mau, Alexander Silva.
items.description_pt: Alquimia. Exposição individual na Usina Luis Maluf, São Paulo (19 outubro – 19 dezembro 2023). Vhils explora a memória coletiva através de registos de luta e utopia, apresentados como imagens deterioradas, fantasmagóricas, que contêm simultaneamente esperança e falência. O título — alquimia — refere-se ao sentimento inexplicável gerado pela união entre pessoas, e aos processos químicos: ácidos e corrosivos que enferrujam e desmantelam camadas de superfície sobre cartazes, paredes, portas e metal. Texto de Julia Flamingo. Fotografias: José Pando Lucas, João Mau, Alexander Silva.

items.title: Interval
items.description: Interval (French title: L'interstice) was a solo exhibition by Alexandre Farto (Vhils) at the Danysz Gallery, 78 rue Amelot, Paris, on view from 22 May to 20 June 2026. Developed through the lens of the "non-places" theorised by anthropologist Marc Augé, the exhibition approached Paris as a city experienced through movement, taking the subway and trains as contemporary spaces of transit. Some twenty-six works spread across the gallery's three floors were made primarily from materials sourced in the French capital, including torn advertising posters, metal political-campaign display structures, subway doors and the city's characteristic ceramic tiles, alongside a painted Lisbon metro carriage body. The presentation surveyed the artist's removal-based techniques, from accumulated and torn posters to carved portraits revealed within the urban crowd.

items.title: Viva la Revolución

items.description: Viva la Revolución: A Dialogue with the Urban Landscape was a group exhibition presented at the Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego from 18 July 2010 to 2 January 2011, gathering twenty artists from eight countries whose practices draw on the codes and icons of the urban environment. Alexandre Farto (Vhils) contributed both gallery and public-site works, including the carved brick-and-plaster wall portrait Scratching the Surface (2010) and two untitled torn-poster street portraits installed at 1202 Kettner Boulevard and at 11th Avenue and Broadway in downtown San Diego. Rather than adding material to surfaces, his works are produced through a reductive process, revealing anonymous portraits by chiselling and tearing away layers of the wall. items.description: Lasco Project #3 was the third iteration of a group program staged in the subterranean passages of the Palais de Tokyo in Paris, curated by Hugo Vitrani and inaugurated in June 2014. This edition marked the internationalisation of the project, bringing together urban artists including Vhils, Futura 2000, Cleon Peterson, Cokney, Horfé, Ken Sortais, Evol, Mode 2, and Lek & Sowat to intervene directly in the building's raw underground spaces. For his contribution Vhils carved an anonymous portrait into the interior surfaces of the Palais de Tokyo, extending his "Scratching the Surface" method of creation through removal. The intervention operated at the threshold between exhibition and urban exploration, examining the political weight of walls and the tension of bringing street practices into an institutional setting.

The presentation formed the second instalment in a sequence of pop-up exhibitions staged by the gallery in the city.
